correctness.rationale: Both equations match the displayed primary models, allowing the stated coordinate names and the affine reciprocal convention for one fiber parameter. I recomputed both discriminants from the binary-quartic invariants I,J using (4I^3-J^2)/27 over F7 and factored the results, independently of the supplied verifier. The finite factor degrees with multiplicities are seven (1,2) and two (4,1) for BT, and seven (1,2) and two (2,2) for AEKS; each degree-22 polynomial adds order two at infinity in the degree-24 section. I checked the nonsquare times irreducible quadratic square at all eight rational parameters for both surfaces, and checked the two residual AEKS square identities with coefficient norms 2 and 4; their common quadratic discriminant is 5, so its roots and both components are defined over F49. A simple discriminant zero has precisely one double root: after splitting coprime root clusters in a strict henselian DVR, a cluster of multiplicity m contributes at least m−1 to the discriminant order (all its root differences have valuation at least 1/m). The simple zero thus gives an irreducible nodal I1. At each double-square fiber the two distinct double-root clusters give two transverse intersections of the rational components, an I2. The models are smooth by the cited constructions; this also follows locally since the discriminant order equals the number of double-root clusters, forcing each quadratic cluster's constant term, after centering at its double root, to have a simple base zero. I evaluated every pair of normalized projective points using a square lookup in two presentations of F49. For BT, the numbers of base pairs lifting to 0, 1 and 2 points are (936,88,1476); for AEKS, (768,144,1588). Thus the counts are 3040 and 3320; both F7 counts are zero. The unequal extension counts obstruct an F7-isomorphism, not necessarily a geometric one.
